<image1>

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Read the following figure, “Profile of Permafrost Distribution in the Northern Hemisphere.” <image1> From west to east across the Eurasian continent, the southern boundary of the permafrost zone distribution shows a pattern of latitude high—low—high; what is its dominant factor?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a “Profile of Permafrost Distribution in the Northern Hemisphere.” The top is marked with latitudes such as about 80°, 70°, 60°, 50°, and 40°. From high latitudes to low latitudes, the permafrost types are shown in sequence as continuous permafrost zone, discontinuous permafrost zone, and seasonal frozen ground zone. The figure also marks the approximate positions of permafrost and its southern boundary. Reasoning: The question stem points out that from west to east across the Eurasian continent, the southern boundary of the permafrost zone distribution shows a “latitude high—low—high” change. The western and eastern parts of the Eurasian continent are more strongly affected by the ocean, and the climate is more obviously maritime; winters are relatively mild, so the southern boundary of permafrost is farther north and at a higher latitude. The central inland region is far from the ocean, has a strong continental climate, and has cold winters, so permafrost can extend toward lower latitudes. Therefore, the dominant factor is the strength of the influence of maritime climate.

raw_record.question_text:
Read the following figure, “Profile of Permafrost Distribution in the Northern Hemisphere.”

<image1>

From west to east across the Eurasian continent, the southern boundary of the permafrost zone distribution shows a pattern of latitude high—low—high; what is its dominant factor?

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: it shows northern-hemisphere permafrost belts arranged from high-latitude continuous permafrost through discontinuous permafrost to seasonal permafrost, with a clear southern boundary. Then read the text: the Eurasian southern boundary changes from high latitude in the west, to low latitude in the middle, then back to high latitude in the east. Match this to Eurasia’s climate pattern: western and eastern margins are more affected by oceans, while the continental interior is less maritime and colder. Therefore the dominant factor is the strength of maritime/oceanic climate influence.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是“北半球多年冻土分布剖面图”，上方标有约80°、70°、60°、50°、40°等纬度，冻土类型从高纬向低纬依次表现为连续多年冻土带、不连续多年冻土带和季节冻土带，图中还标出了多年冻土及其南界大致位置。推理：题干指出亚欧大陆自西向东冻土带分布南界呈现“纬度高—低—高”的变化。亚欧大陆西部和东部受海洋影响较强，气候海洋性较明显，冬季相对温和，多年冻土南界偏北、纬度较高；中部内陆远离海洋，气候大陆性强，冬季寒冷，多年冻土可向较低纬度扩展。因此主导因素是海洋性气候影响强弱。
